description: Historical chronicle manuscript documented in Pacific Linguistics 565 (p. 410), recording the royal lineage of the Tai people from celestial ancestor Chaw Tai Lung across Upper Burma through the 13th-century Patkai crossing of Prince Sukapha into the Brahmaputra valley.

full_translation: Chaw Tai Lung was the exalted ancestor from whom the great Tai lineages trace their origin. They founded mighty realms along the fertile Shweli (Nam Mau) before migrating toward the Patkai. In 1228 AD, Prince Chau Lung Sukapha led his followers across the Patkai into the plains of Upper Assam. The Nora (Khamyang) and the Ahoms lived as elder and younger brothers under one ancestral bond. This ancestral Buranji chronicle is preserved as an everlasting beacon of Tai history and courage.
